newsitem.title: POLAND: HALF OF POLISH MASS PRIVATISATION UNITS RESOLD.
newsitem.headline: HALF OF POLISH MASS PRIVATISATION UNITS RESOLD.

text.p: Nearly 50 percent of Poles who bought mass privatisation units sold them on the secondary market, according to a survey released on Thursday.

The survey by the private Demoskop agency showed that 65 percent of those who sold their units were people below 24 year of age. Units were also frequently sold by the unemployed, poorly paid and those with low education.
The poll indicated that 23 percent of those who bought the units planned to keep them and seven percent wanted to sell them in near future.
About 47 percent thought the unit was good investment while 23 percent did not think so. About 30 percent said they had no opinion.
The poll, with a 3.2-percent error margin, was carried out among a representative group of 990 adults in November 8-12.
Since the start of the sale in 1995, Poles bought more than 24 million units.
The sale ends on Friday and many of the remaining four million eligible buyers queue for many hours to get their unit.
The National Investment Fund (NFI) units are sold under a programme allowing each adult Pole to buy one such coupon for 20 zlotys.
The unit will later be exchanged for shares in each of the 15 NFIs, grouping more than 500 firms undergoing privatisation.
The NFI unit is traded at about 150 zlotys on the Warsaw stock exchange.
